text:
elena: Heads-up — nightly perf dash alerted ~20% throughput drop on the v2-serving pool starting 00:10 UTC, looks correlated with 03/14 release window. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/boards/nightly/v2-serving
marcus: saw that, tail latency also spiked. Which metric triggered?
elena: 'throughput_per_gpu' dip + 'p95_latency' up. Alert: Nightly Regression — throughput down 18%, p95 +42%.
jia: I just checked CI perf history for the merge window — perf-experiment job #perf-2027 shows a reg at commit abcdef1 (PR #4421).
ben: PR #4421 was the KV-cache eviction rework (LRU->clock) and prefetch hint tweak, landed in runtime/core last night.
marcus: that matches. Any flamegraphs or perf profiles from the night run?
elena: uploaded a snapshot: flame_v2_00.tar.gz (s3://artifacts/nightly/3441200000/flame). Quick diff shows increased time in kv_cache::lookup and kernel_selector stall.
nora: small note: kernel selection calls are blocking while waiting on KV miss prefetch now — we changed prefetch semaphore order in the PR.
sam: can we reproduce locally? Running local nightly harness with a replay of typical traffic now (batch sizes, seq len distro).
opsbot: nightly-bisect started (job: bisect-nightly-3441200000).
sam: repro confirmed on my harness: throughput -21%, p95 +38%. Added perf record.
ben: quick grep in PR shows we flipped 'reorder_on_touch = true' in runtime/core/kv_cache.cc; old behavior kept stable hotset ordering. Code snippet: ```// before: reorder_on_touch = false; // after: reorder_on_touch = true```
marcus: that would cause frequent reshuffle of hot slots under certain access patterns, can thrash the cache and cause misses.
jia: CI perf job also shows kernel selector doing more probing: kernel_selector::probe_count +3x, likely because KV miss forces kernels to fallback.
elena: bisect bot says candidate commit is abcdef1 -> 1.2.8-release-merge. Anyone object to holding the release?
ben: hold it. This is a clear regression for production latency.
ora: I've flagged rollout to 'hold' in console and notified infra SRE.
deploy-bot: rollout status: HOLD applied by nora.
sam: temporary mitigation idea: revert reorder_on_touch change or toggle it off via runtime flag (kv.reorder_on_touch=false). Do we have a dynamic flag?
ben: added a dynamic flag in the PR but default flipped. We can flip it back without a full revert. I can push a hotfix patch to revert default to false.
marcus: prefer hotfix revert-to-default and run a quick canary instead of full revert.
jia: I ran the hotfix locally (flip flag) and saw throughput recover to within 3% of baseline, p95 back down.
elena: good. Ben, can you open a patch and a rollback changelog?
ben: created PR #4430 — runtime: set kv.reorder_on_touch default=false, includes test and a canary rollout policy. Link: https://git.redwood/pr/4430
opsbot: canary-deploy started (canary: v2-serving-hotfix-4430).
marcus: monitoring canary now — initial 10 minutes look stable. p50/p95 within normal.
ora: please also capture KV cache histograms and eviction counters for 30m window.
sam: attaching short logs from local perf run: ```KV misses/sec: before 120 -> after 18; kernel probe stalls/sec: before 45 -> after 5```
elena: CI perf job re-run scheduled on #perf-2027 with patch applied.
jia: note for postmortem: workload sensitivity test uncovered this — we should add a microbenchmark that stresses 'touch-heavy' hotset patterns to prevent regression.
ben: Agreed. I'll add a test in perf harness and a gating CI job for kv_cache heuristics.
marcus: long-term: revisit clock vs lru tradeoffs but only with perf proof on our tenant workloads.
elena: closing loop: canary looks good for 20m, infra approved rollback to stable. Rolling back release + creating incident doc.
deploy-bot: rollout status: ROLLBACK initiated by nora -> complete.
opsbot: nightly-bisect job finished: root cause pinned to commit abcdef1 (PR #4421).
elena: thanks all — follow-up actions: 1) merge hotfix #4430, 2) add targeted perf test, 3) postmortem draft in /incidents. I'll start the incident doc.
ben: will merge hotfix after one more thumbs up. :thumbsup:
marcus: thumbs.
jia: adding regression alert rule change to include kernel_selector probe_count in future alerts.
elena: great. I'll update the dashboard notebook with annotated regression markers.
opsbot: incident created: INCIDENT-2026-03-KV-WARMUP.
elena: end thread.
